display_name: The Misuse of Drugs Act 1973: the offences (controlled drugs and psychoactive substances), the presumptions and evidence rules, the powers of search, arrest and specimen, forfeiture, jurisdiction, and every punishment (the Second Schedule's table in full, ss 33, 33A, 33B)
scope: The Misuse of Drugs Act 1973 as printed in SSO's PDF, current version as at 01 Oct 2026: the offences of Parts 2, 2A and 2B (ss 5 to 14, 11A to 11Q) with the definitions they turn on (s 2) and the proof of a psychoactive substance (ss 22A, 22B); the presumptions and evidence rules (ss 15 to 23, 31(6), 33(4AC) to (4AE), 33A(3), (4)); the powers of search, arrest, urine, hair and oral fluid specimens, and forfeiture (ss 24 to 28, 30 to 32); jurisdiction (s 53) and a statement to the Criminal Procedure Code 2010 about the Act's offences (ss 25(1), 53); and every punishment: the Second Schedule's printed table in full (86 rows, generated), ss 33, 33A and 33B, and the punishments the other sections state (49 rows). NOT encoded: the lists of substances in the First, Third and Fifth Schedules (the class of a drug, and whether a thing is a controlled drug, are inputs); treatment and rehabilitation (ss 34 to 39) apart from the antecedent facts they supply; photographs and body samples (ss 40A to 40D); committees of inquiry (ss 41 to 52); ss 26A and 29 (disposal of seized and forfeited things); ss 54 to 57; regulations (ss 10B, 58, 59).

not_reviewed.note: No domain expert has read this against the Act. An independent test pass was run on 2026-10-01 (tests-independent.l4, 315 assertions, no disagreement; its author read the Second Schedule from the printed page and found no mismatch in the cells it tested), but it read the modules for names and signatures and is not a substitute for expert review. The Second Schedule table was transcribed twice by the same session, once into generators/mda_schedule.py and once, as the printed words, into generators/mda_tests_2.py, and the thresholds were checked against the text. The source is SSO's unofficial consolidation. NOTES.md sections 7 to 10.

forks.F1: The substance lists of the First, Third and Fifth Schedules are not carried: the class of a drug, and 'is a controlled drug', 'is within the Third Schedule', 'is within another paragraph of the Fifth Schedule' are inputs.
forks.F2: A controlled drug is never a psychoactive substance (Fifth Schedule para 4 excludes any controlled drug or controlled substance), so Part 2 and Part 2A offences cannot both be made out on one thing.
forks.F3: A presumption's outcome (ss 17 to 22) is a BOOLEAN input to the offence rules; the accused's rebuttal is a fact and its standard is not encoded.
forks.F4: Second Schedule, sixth column: where one drug engages two rows that print different punishments the answer is REFUSE; an opium band needs both its weight and its morphine content, so opium in the weight band without the morphine content falls to the class column.
forks.F5: Class-column rows 'except as otherwise provided in this Schedule' and the sixth-column possession row 8(a)(9) are residual: they apply only when no specific sixth-column row is engaged.
forks.F6: An offence under s 8(b), 31(2) or 31A(2) committed before 1 April 2019 is REFUSE: s 33(3A) applies only from that date and the Act as it then stood is not encoded. s 33(4) prints no maximum, and the row's maximum is 0, 'none printed'.
forks.F7: s 53: the Act's statement to the Code says a District Court may try its offences and a Magistrate's Court may not; 'jurisdiction to hear and determine all proceedings' is read as proceedings within a Magistrate's Court's sentencing powers, which the Code decides.
forks.F8: Repeat and enhanced bands in the sections (11B to 11Q, 33(3B), 33(3D), 33(4A) to (4C)) are engaged by facts the caller supplies; only the antecedent counts of ss 33A and 33(4) to (4AB) are computed.
forks.F9: s 11P(9)(b), (c): the belief defence is applied to every activity except consuming alone.
forks.F10: ss 5(2), 11F(2): possession for the purpose of trafficking is trafficking; the s 17 presumption stands for that element and is an input.
forks.F11: s 20: the presumption is about the drug's import with the master's knowledge and is not limited to the accused being the master.
forks.F12: s 24 names a SENIOR officer of customs; ss 25 and 26 name any officer of customs; kept as the Act has them.
